transcript:
maya: Heads-up — we're finalizing the KMS design for a Redwood Private VPC customer. Need a quick sanity check: control plane keys vs dataplane keys, rotation cadence, grant patterns for cross-account deploy agents, and audit/tracing requirements. Any red flags?

oliver: +1 on separating KEK (control plane) and DEKs (dataplane). Control plane KMS keys should be in customer's account (BYOK) when requested; data-plane DEKs can be customer account or our service account depending on trust model.

samir: For dataplane perf we cache unwrapped DEKs for active replica lifetimes. We use envelope encryption: generate DEK (AES-256-GCM), wrap with customer CMK via KMS Encrypt, store wrapped_dek in metadata store. Cache decrypted DEK in memory with TTL. Keep TTL << CMK rotation window.

arjun: Rotation plan: rewrap DEKs when KEK rotates. Ops: run a background rewrap job that pulls wrapped_dek, calls ReEncrypt (or Decrypt + Encrypt) with new CMK, store new wrapped_dek. Schedule can be phased per-customer to avoid API/QPS spikes.

maya: Q: Do we use Grant tokens or IAM grants for the runtime service principal? Concerns about least-privilege and rotating principals.

oliver: Prefer IAM roles with key policy + condition restricting kms:ViaService or source VPC when possible. Grants are useful for short-lived cross-account access (e.g., one-off bootstrap) but have caveats: expire on key deletion, and listing grants is limited.

samir: Implementation note: when we decrypt DEKs on worker nodes we should use KMS Decrypt with GrantToken only during bootstrap. After that, avoid long-lived grants; use IAM role perms for steady-state decrypts to prevent stale grant issues.

security-bot: Reminder: enable CloudTrail Data Events for KMS in the customer's account to capture Encrypt/Decrypt/ReEncrypt calls. Forward logs to central audit S3 + Datadog. Retention per compliance: 7 years for SOC2 customers by default.

oncall: Incident scenario — if customer's CMK gets disabled accidentally (human error), we need fallback path: 1) fail open? NO. 2) Promote a fallback CMK (customer-approved) and trigger rewrap using key rotation job. Notify customer + auto-rollback plan documented.

arjun: Add to runbook: healthcheck that detects spikes in KMS ThrottlingException and automatically slow-roll rewraps + queue backoff. Metrics: KMS ThrottleRate, latency P90 for Decrypt, ReEncrypt job error rate.

maya: RBAC ask: product wants ability to grant read-only audit access to customer's security team — what minimal IAM policy to view CloudTrail + KMS key metadata without key usage?

oliver: Provide a policy that allows cloudtrail:LookupEvents, s3:GetObject on audit bucket prefix, kms:DescribeKey and kms:GetKeyRotationStatus but NOT kms:Decrypt|Encrypt. Also restrict to specific ARNs.

samir: Ops-level snippet for rewrap (AWS CLI):
```
aws kms re-encrypt \
  --ciphertext-blob fileb://wrapped_dek.bin \
  --destination-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/NEW-KEY-ID \
  --source-encryption-context "customer_id=acme"
```
If ReEncrypt not available (old SDK), do Decrypt -> Encrypt.

maya: Thanks — last Q: audit trail correlation. We need to map a KMS Encrypt/Decrypt call to a Redwood request id. Best practice?

oliver: Include request_id in the EncryptionContext when calling KMS. KMS logs include the encryption context in CloudTrail. Example: EncryptionContext={"request_id":"r-123","customer":"acme","purpose":"dataplane-dek-wrap"}

security-bot: Also enforce tagging of KMS keys with customer id and environment so searches are easier.

oncall: One more—test plan for rotation: unit test for rewrap logic, chaostest that disables key then runs restore flow, and DR tabletop for CMK compromise (revoke + rewrap all, customer notification templates).

maya: Perfect — I'll update the design doc and add these runbook items. TY all :tada!
